content: Edarbi is a prescription medication classified as an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB). It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults. Your doctor may prescribe additional medications to be taken alongside Edarbi to help manage your high blood pressure. However, the safety and effectiveness of Edarbi in children under 18 years of age have not been established. Before starting Edarbi, inform your doctor if you have been diagnosed with abnormal levels of body salts (electrolytes) in your blood. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to breastfeed. It is not known whether Edarbi passes into breast milk. You and your doctor should decide whether you will take Edarbi or breastfeed, but you should not do both. Discuss the best feeding options for your baby with your doctor if you are taking Edarbi. Inform your doctor about all medications you are currently taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements. This includes other medications used to treat high blood pressure or heart problems, as well as diuretics (water pills). If you are unsure whether you are taking any of these medications, consult your doctor. Keep a list of all your medications and share it with your doctor or pharmacist when starting a new medication. Your doctor will provide specific instructions on how much Edarbi to take and when to take it. Follow these instructions carefully. Edarbi can be taken with or without food. If you accidentally take too much Edarbi, contact your doctor or go to the nearest hospital emergency room immediately. Edarbi may cause side effects, including harm or death to an unborn fetus if taken during the second or third trimester of pregnancy. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, consult your doctor immediately. Edarbi may also cause low blood pressure (hypotension) and dizziness, particularly if you are taking diuretics, following a low-salt diet, taking other medications that affect blood pressure, experiencing vomiting or diarrhea, or not drinking enough fluids. If you feel faint or dizzy, lie down and contact your doctor right away. These are not all the possible side effects of Edarbi. Inform your doctor if you experience any side effects that bother you or do not go away. For medical advice about side effects, contact your doctor. You can also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088. Store Edarbi at a temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in the original container provided by your pharmacist or doctor, and do not transfer it to another container. Ensure the container is tightly closed and protected from light. Medications are sometimes prescribed for purposes other than those listed in the patient information leaflet. Do not share Edarbi with others, even if they have the same symptoms as you, as it may harm them. This patient information leaflet summarizes the most important details about Edarbi. For more information, consult your doctor or pharmacist. You can also request information written for healthcare professionals. High blood pressure occurs when the force of blood against the walls of your blood vessels is too high. This condition makes the heart work harder to pump blood and can damage blood vessels. Edarbi tablets help relax your blood vessels, lowering your blood pressure. Medications that lower blood pressure may reduce your risk of stroke or heart attack. The active ingredient in Edarbi is azilsartan medoxomil. Inactive ingredients include mannitol, fumaric acid, sodium hydroxide, hydroxypropyl cellulose, croscarmellose sodium, microcrystalline cellulose, and magnesium stearate. If you consume alcohol, discuss with your doctor the potential effects of alcohol when taking this medication, as the interaction between alcohol and azilsartan medoxomil has not been established.
